results.title: Expected after India’s Ladakh naming, the FM’s trade-barrier callouts & tighter FDI PN3 scrutiny for China.
results.description:
Expected after India’s Ladakh naming, the FM’s trade-barrier callouts & tighter FDI PN3 scrutiny for China.

Chinese are posturing. Beijing rarely imposes permanent bans; expect waivers. Licensing bottlenecks create uncertain lead times for Indian EPC contractors pricing Chinese equip—next 'case-by-case' waivers may force contractors to disclose precise project locations & site data to MOFCOM to prove "non-military" use.

Bottomline: suit up & invest—or suck up and stop the border posturing without sufficient leverage.

results.title: China’s export controls on tunnel-boring machines are more significant than they first appear.
results.description:
China’s export controls on tunnel-boring machines are more significant than they first appear.

These are not ordinary consumer goods. They are strategic infrastructure equipment.

For years, Chinese netizens have questioned why China should supply machinery that can strengthen Indian infrastructure near the China-India border while New Delhi simultaneously uses roads, tunnels and forward construction to alter the military balance there.

The contradiction was obvious:

China cannot treat strategic industrial capacity as politically neutral when that same capacity can be used to strengthen infrastructure directed against China’s own security interests.

Export licensing does not mean “no exports.”
It means Beijing is finally drawing a line between commercial trade and unconditional access to strategic capability.

China spent decades building the world’s most formidable industrial toolbox.

It is now learning that not every tool needs to be handed to everyone who asks.
